clue.text: Way of working, possibly pseudorandom one

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters could be arranged another way, so they get reshuffled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone describes a working method as perhaps a random-looking one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' tells you to rearrange PSEUDORANDOM; then add I (one) at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used in English for a habitual method or procedure for doing something.

clue.text: Moderately quiet about a plan

indicators.note: 'about' means the MP letters go around the a

parts.note: mp, mezzo piano, is the musical marking for moderately quiet

explanation.surface: Someone is quietly thinking about a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: MP is the musical direction mezzo piano, moderately soft; it goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A map is a layout or diagram, as in mapping out a scheme, so it is a synonym for a plan.

clue.text: British scientist: one cuts eccentric figure, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the result is read backwards
'cuts' has the one slicing into the middle of the eccentric figure

parts.note: a card is an amusing, eccentric person
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A British scientist, on thinking it over, seems an odd figure.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into CARD to make CARID, and 'on reflection' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dirac was the English theoretical physicist who shared the 1933 Nobel Prize for quantum mechanics.

clue.text: Ostentatious agent receiving cruel punishment

indicators.note: 'receiving' has the agent taking in the punishment between his letters

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
the lash is a whipping, a cruel punishment

explanation.surface: A showy secret agent ends up being whipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Splashy means flashy and attention-seeking, the same idea as showy display.

clue.text: Request funding — spare thousand, potentially? Half of that secured

indicators.note: 'secured' has the shuffled letters holding the half-word inside them
'potentially' says these letters could become something else, so they are rearranged
the first half of the word 'that' is taken

explanation.surface: Someone asks for money: could you spare a thousand, or even half that?
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange SPARE and THOUSAND ('potentially'), and fit TH, the first half of 'that', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing round a hat is the idiom for collecting donations from a group of people.

clue.text: Board supporting artist, subject to local charges

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a table is a board, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A board backing an artist turns out to be liable for council tax.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for a member of Britain's Royal Academy. Rates were the British local property tax, which is what 'local charges' refers to.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratable property is one assessed for rates, the old British local property tax.

clue.text: Military rifle to annoy Rev

parts.note: to needle someone is to annoy them
to rev an engine is to gun it

explanation.surface: A soldier's rifle is used to irritate a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev' looks like the clergyman's title, but it is the verb: to gun an engine is to rev it.
explanation.definitionFit: The needle gun was a nineteenth-century Prussian breech-loading rifle fired by a needle-like pin.

clue.text: I'm a US soldier encountering local resident, coming up with new ideas

parts.note: taken as written, without its apostrophe
a GI is an American soldier
a native is someone living where they were born

explanation.surface: An American soldier says he is meeting a local and getting fresh thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: An imaginative person is inventive and creative, always producing original thoughts.

clue.text: Almost certain to seize power, having encouragement

indicators.note: 'to seize' has the shortened word gripping the power letter
'Almost' means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: sure means certain
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone almost sure to take power is buoyed by encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: SURE loses its last letter ('Almost') to give SUR, which takes P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is literally a rider's goad, so figuratively an incentive or stimulus.

clue.text: Go off track? Soprano finally prepared to cut into song

indicators.note: 'into' places the three pieces inside the song

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or song

indicators.note: 'finally' takes the last letter of soprano

parts.note: set means prepared, ready
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: A soprano, ready at last, is cutting into a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut into song' looks like one phrase, but 'to cut' is its own piece and 'into' is the container signal; a lay is an old word for a ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose the way is to stray from the right route, getting lost or off course.

clue.text: A defender short? Our team is something that counts

indicators.note: 'short' cuts off the last letter

parts.note: a back is a defender in football
us is our team, ourselves

explanation.surface: A football fan complains that the team is a defender short.
explanation.walkthrough: BACK loses its last letter to give BAC.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a counting frame of beads on rods, a device for doing arithmetic.

clue.text: Finds place to stay for party and wife — and their correspondence?

parts.note: to billet soldiers is to find them lodgings
a do is a party
ux is short for Latin uxor, wife

explanation.surface: Someone finds lodgings for a party and a wife, and wonders what letters they write.
explanation.walkthrough: UX, from Latin uxor, is the abbreviation for wife used in legal documents. 'their' points to a party and wife as a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Billets-doux are love letters, the correspondence exchanged between sweethearts.

clue.text: French writer presenting a book in form of serial

indicators.note: 'in' puts the a and book inside the reshaped letters
'form of' means a new shape is made from the letters

explanation.surface: A French author offers a book in instalments.
explanation.walkthrough: SERIAL rearranged ('form of') becomes RELAIS, and A plus B go in after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Francois Rabelais was the French Renaissance author of Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: Response to sneeze not so much unknown during endless period of illness

indicators.note: 'during' places these within the shortened illness
'endless' cuts off the final letter

parts.note: a bout is a spell of illness
less means not so much
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone who sneezes during a long bout of sickness gets a less heartfelt reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so much' and 'unknown' look like commentary on the reply, but both are pieces; Y as an unknown comes from algebra.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'bless you' is the customary polite reply when somebody sneezes.

clue.text: Hit the heights, welcoming religious leader on to a TV show?

indicators.note: 'on to' attaches the result to the a, which comes after it
'welcoming' has the soaring word take in the religious leader

parts.note: to soar is to fly high
the Pope leads the Catholic church

explanation.surface: A pope rises to fame by going on a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: The religious leader goes between the A and R of the soaring word, not at its edge, and 'on to a' then adds the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama broadcast on television or radio.

clue.text: Memory trace? Recalled shock about old King

indicators.note: 'about' places the turned word around the king
'Recalled' means called back, so the word is turned around

parts.note: a shock of hair is a mane
GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A trace in someone's memory brings back a shock about an old monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' is the hair, not the fright. GR, Georgius Rex, is Latin for King George, seen on British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: An engram is the hypothetical physical change in the brain thought to store a memory.

clue.text: Inclines to invest millions in race venue

indicators.note: 'to invest' in the old sense of to surround: the inclines wrap around the millions

parts.note: to lean is to incline
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to put millions into a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Mans in France hosts the famous 24-hour motor race.

clue.text: Look quickly over, then enquire for winter sports item

parts.note: to skim a text is to glance over it
to ask is to enquire

explanation.surface: Someone glances over a catalogue, then asks about skiing gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski mask is a knitted face covering worn by skiers against the cold.

clue.text: Elegant new member of Society broadcasting

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a young woman entering high society
on air means being broadcast

explanation.surface: A stylish young society newcomer appears on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave, stylish and charming in manner.

clue.text: Strange vulgar business arranged with European in support

indicators.note: in a down clue the support sits below, so the European letter comes last

parts.note: biz is slang, a vulgar form, for business
arr. is the musical abbreviation for arranged

explanation.surface: A crude business deal arranged with a European backer looks odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre means very odd or weird in appearance or behaviour.

clue.text: A boy is hot, sustaining temperature? Wow

indicators.note: 'sustaining' has the boy holding the temperature letter inside

parts.note: a son is a boy
H is the abbreviation for hot, on taps

explanation.surface: A feverish boy is holding a high temperature, to everyone's amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: To wow someone is to amaze or impress them greatly, a verb sense.

clue.text: Spot that woman's stringed instrument

parts.note: a zit is a pimple, a spot
her means that woman's

explanation.surface: Someone spots a woman's stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a verb meaning notice; it is the noun, a pimple.
explanation.definitionFit: A zither is a flat stringed instrument plucked across a soundbox.

clue.text: Suggestion about trimmed bulb for flower

indicators.note: 'about' has the suggestion go around the trimmed letters

parts.note: a tip is a suggestion or hint

indicators.note: 'trimmed' cuts both ends off the word bulb

explanation.surface: Advice about trimming a bulb so it flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bulb trimmed of its ends leaves UL, which TIP surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a spring-blooming plant grown from a bulb, with cup-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Ancestor's warning: destiny involving hard year ultimately

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning cry

indicators.note: 'involving' has destiny wrap around the hard letter

parts.note: fate is destiny
H is the abbreviation for hard, on pencils

indicators.note: 'ultimately' takes the last letter of year

explanation.surface: An ancestor cries a warning about a destiny with a hard year at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fore' is the shout golfers give to warn others of an incoming ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A forefather is a forebear, a person from whom one is descended.

clue.text: Spoils good deal, doubling content

indicators.note: 'doubling' means a second copy of that middle letter goes in beside the first

parts.note: a lot is a good deal, a large amount
the content of the good-deal word is its middle letter, O

explanation.surface: Someone spoils a good deal by doubling what goes in.
explanation.walkthrough: The O in the middle of LOT is doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is plunder, the goods taken in war or by thieves, i.e. spoils.

clue.text: Porter dropping stone is dismissed

indicators.note: 'dropping' means the stone letters are removed

parts.note: porter and stout are both dark beers
st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A porter who drops a stone is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a doorman, but it is the beer: a stout is a strong porter. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out.

clue.text: Treasure instruction that's provided by Times?

definitions.text: Treasure instruction that's provided by Times?

parts.words: Treasure instruction that's provided by Times?
parts.note: the treasure-map phrase, read as the multiplication sign (the times symbol) marking a location

explanation.walkthrough: Times here is not the newspaper: the multiplication sign is a cross, the letter that marks the spot on a treasure map.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the classic pirate-map direction saying where buried treasure lies.
